body:
I once heard a retired rock star say in an interview that his biggest regret was that he got into drugs. He also said that the criteria to follow for determining when to quit were when the negatives outweighed the positives.
Its funny how much more clearly I understand both of those statements, now.
I consider myself a seasoned drug user. And, while I dont regret having done these things, I know they have permanently changed who I am
With nothing more than a grin and an idea, I said that I wanted to become a drug kingpin. It took less than 12 months.
Preview:
The first summer I consumed MDMA, I got high on it a handful of times over the course of the summer months, maybe 5 times. It was love. The sun was always bright, and life was good. It was such a beautiful contribution to life. A contribution to life. Like an ice cold coca cola, you know? It was that simple. The reward to cost ratio was through the roof.
By the time September arrived, I was receiving packages of 1000s in the mail. Well, at first it was 500, and then 1000, then 1000s. It was just good capitalism. Why spend $150 and be a consumer for a weekend when
I could spend $1500, and be the supplier forever, hypothetically. By the next summer, I was partying (living) off the profit, and getting high every weekend. Often times on consecutive days. I gave away much more than I ever spent/used. I provided for several people for many months. I think at one point I was making over $20,000/month, and kept my hands clean. I traveled to Europe. I made many memories. I value all of these memories. And still, I can tell you that it was not worth it.
Somewhere between being happy and having fun, to becoming a large-scale drug dealer knowing that life in prison was en route via the post, the highs stopped being pleasurable.  I learned that my friends werent real. And, all the good times I had were an illusion. Eventually the highs with minimal comedowns gave way to nightlong paranoia & anxiety, and a week of depression afterward. Try doing your homework knowing that life in prison will show up in your mailbox at any moment.
And yet, I would keep getting high with the memories of how good it had been. Trying to feel that love again. I cant remember the last time the high was what I had hoped for.
But, the paranoia took over my life.
the paranoia took over my life.
It first started out from becoming sensitive to undercover cops in the clubs. That is, me being high and suddenly becoming hyper aware of a suspicious person. The people that are clearly sober, not enjoying the music, looking, steering an unsolicited conversation to molly - rude. I started suspecting everyone was a police informant, or an undercover cop. My phone is definitely being monitored. Theyre building evidence and just waiting for me to make a mistake. Obviously. Trying to convince my friends that theres an undercover cop in the club and hes following me. Meanwhile, word gets out that one of the friends has been arrested for dealing. Hm. Paranoid, or observant? Im still free, either way. Call me crazy if you like.
Getting to the point:
I will be a proponent of drug legalization and fight draconian drug laws to the day I die. But, like I said, I understand why drugs are illegal, and I think my journey with drugs is over.
Rest assured that
once I started doing drugs regularly, I associated with bad people. And if you are a good person - A tourist in the underworld  you will learn very quickly of the dangers. Bad People have no moral compass, or concern about how their actions put your life at risk. Your life.
Leading to the next point. The worst part of it all is that any social connection I made was not true. That was always the hardest part for me to overcome. I believed that the love was real. That these people cared about me. Bad people care about themselves, first, and me, second, assuming I can do something for them. For many of these people, there is no tomorrow. They dont have plans for the future. Why would I ever think that they would care about my plans for the future?
Business Case:
I want to present the business case for dealing drugs, and show why it is not worth it.
Firstly, being convicted of trafficking (importing) MDMA into the USA has a guideline sentence of life in prison. If you got convicted of selling large quantities, the guideline sentence is 15 years per count. Ok. So Life. Your Life. In prison. For the rest of your life.
Wait a second, Im the idiot for going that far. Why bother going to that scale? Well, you see, the scales of economy are very steep for drugs, and there are many ancillary costs. One pill is $20-$30 per pill. One Hundred Pills that price falls to around $10 per pill. By the time you reach 5000 pills, the cost is below $3. Three dollars. For Pure MDMA, its $24 per gram. For methylone, bk-MDMA, its $2 per gram, at the kilo level.
Now, think about costs. The true costs.  Well, I leave the operation costs out. But, Ill tell you. I needed at least 400% in revenue to maintain my
level of operation. Holy Shit, what? Yeah. So if I bought 1000 pills for $5000, thats a $5 cost, I need to sell them all at $20 to cover all the costs of precaution, travel, packing material, live, and have enough to resupply. But wait, there are more costs
What would I do if I actually got caught? I wouldnt even have enough money to retain an attorney, or post bail. How much would I be willing to pay to be free? Think about it. Even if I could sell at $60 a pill, the stress on my mental health wouldnt be worth it, let alone the risk to my freedom. The only way to actually make enough is to buy many thousands.
Was I really willing to throw the rest of  life away to become a drug kingpin?
Im lucky. I included the person I thought was a friend. I taught him everything, and even gave him my contact in Amsterdam. It was a beautiful business. But, like I said. Bad peopleIt was less than 6 months that I was removed from operations. Lucky me. The second I realized it, I told myself it was a blessing in disguise. Im still here.
Have you ever seen Blow with Johnny Depp? You could say that I expected that to happen when I brought him in. My friends corruption was my exit strategy.
On the other hand, as the consumer, you could be making a bad person rich. I provided top quality gear, but many people buy the fake drug, and cut it. So, you might be paying $100 for a gram that cost him $2, and he cut the gram with some other drug. Youre giving him 5000% profit for causing your body harm. Why would you be willing to give this person a living? Why would you be willing to do that to your body?
So, back to the point of losing the magic:
Its a weird feeling to be high on ecstasy, and not enjoy it. I still feel good, and I can look into another persons eyes and instantly fall in love. But, it was different before.  It used to be so good that I needed to rub some extra love onto others, whereas now I cant tellif I'm happy orless happy?
now I cant tellif I'm happy orless happy?
I cant remember the last time I watched Blow, but it is very appropriate.  The feeling of loneliness is perfectly articulated.
Depp: So in the end, was it worth it? Jesus Christ. How irreparably changed my life has become. It's always the last day of summer and I've been left out in the cold with no door to get back in. I'll grant you I've had more than my share of poignant moments. Life passes most people by while they're making grand plans for it. Throughout my lifetime, I've left pieces of my heart here and there. And now, there's almost not enough to stay alive. But I force a smile, knowing that my ambition far exceeded my talent. There are no more white horses or pretty ladies at my door.
I'd also like to say that police do an important job in society. But pursuing drug users is not one of them.
